## 2. Technical functionality and algorithms

**Data and cohort.** The released file ({records} records) is read only after its SHA 256 matches the frozen value. Pure parsers turn text cells into typed values: blood pressure is read with a regular expression that takes the first pair of two or three digit numbers around a slash, a sentinel policy turns tokens such as "not_checked" into missing values, and a numeric parser repairs unambiguous slips such as a trailing full stop. Values outside the physiological ranges of `StudySpec` become missing and the record is kept. `CohortBuilder` then applies one named method per eligibility step and records the step and reason for every excluded record, giving the eligible cohort of {eligible} and the analysis cohort of {analysis_cohort} pregnancies with {analysis_events} low birth weight births.

**Grouped stratified partitioning.** Records that share a registration profile (age, last menstrual date, height, registration weight and prior deliveries) form a group. A stratified group split assigns whole groups to folds while balancing events; its first fold is the held out partition of {holdout_n} pregnancies with {holdout_events} events, written to file with a checksum before any screen or model step and readable only through a gate that logs every attempt. The development partition holds {dev_n} pregnancies with {dev_events} events.

**Feature sets.** Set A holds registration characteristics, set B adds the visit two measurements, and set C adds the visit one value of each measurement recorded at both visits for at least {availability_percent} percent of records. The availability screen never reads the outcome and is refitted in every training fold. For a linear model the change between visits is an exact linear combination of the two values, so set C adds values only; tree models also receive the change. Sets are subclasses of one abstract `FeatureSet`, so the runner never branches on a set's name.

**Models.** {families} families (L2 and L1 logistic regression, linear discriminant analysis, nearest neighbours, naive Bayes, a decision tree, a random forest and gradient boosted trees) and a constant prevalence baseline. Every pipeline imputes medians with a missingness indicator and scales where needed, except the gradient boosted trees, which handle missing values natively. No class weighting or resampling is used, so probabilities stay on the natural scale.

**Nested cross validation.** {outer_folds} outer folds repeated {repeats} times, with hyperparameters chosen in {inner_folds} grouped inner folds by average precision. Outer test records take no part in any choice, and predictions are stored per record per repeat.

**Paired group bootstrap.** Predictions are averaged per pregnancy across repeats, the paired difference in a metric between two feature sets is computed on the same pregnancies, and registration groups are resampled {resamples} times to give a percentile interval. The bootstrap standard error gives the smallest detectable difference, (z for a two sided five percent test plus z for 80 percent power) times the standard error.

**Interval on one probability.** For the served L2 logistic model the coefficient covariance is the inverse of the penalised Hessian of the fitted design matrix. For a new case the standard error of the logit is computed from that covariance, and the Wald interval is transformed to the probability scale. It describes uncertainty in the estimate, not in the outcome.

**Decision curve and retrieval.** Net benefit counts true positives minus false positives weighted by the threshold odds. Retrieval reports the share of events in the top of the ranking against random ranking.

**Data model.** `python -m antenatal load-db` writes the research side of the proposal's data model into the application's SQLite file: pregnancy records with their eligibility and exclusion reason, cleaned visit measurements unique on record and visit number, the frozen model configurations, and every outer fold result unique on model, feature set, repeat and fold. The prototype's synthetic cases, visits and assessments sit in the same file. No table records which records are held out.

**Prototype.** A FastAPI application whose routers validate and route, whose services decide, and whose database stores synthetic cases, visits and assessments. Scoring goes only through the frozen artefact, whose checksum is verified when the application starts; a changed file stops the server. The interface shows rank, probability, the labelled interval, prevalence, event count, artefact version and a fixed limitation line, and never a risk category.

## 4. Code quality practices

The package separates data access, parsing, cohort rules, partitioning, features, models, evaluation, the artefact and reporting into their own modules, and every constant lives in one frozen `StudySpec`. Abstraction and polymorphism are used where there is more than one implementation: `FeatureSet` with its subclasses, and `MetricStrategy` with one subclass per metric. Every public class and function has a docstring and type hints. No function exceeds 50 lines and no file exceeds 300 lines, checked by a script. Ruff and black run locally and in the continuous integration workflow, every output file carries a checksum in `outputs/manifest.json`, and the README results and tree are generated and checked by a test. The history holds {commits} commits, each with an imperative message stating what changed and why.

| Share of events in the top 10, 20 and 30 percent of the ranking | {retrieval10}; {retrieval20}; {retrieval30} |
| Pulse missing minus recorded, low birth weight rate | {pulse_diff} |

**Reading.** Adding the first visit to the second did not improve prediction of recorded low birth weight by any amount this design could detect, in either model family, in any sensitivity analysis, under multiple imputation, or at any training size on the learning curve. The second visit over registration alone shows weak evidence of a gain in discrimination, with an interval excluding zero for the tree model but not for logistic regression. The predicted probabilities are calibrated within their uncertainty. Ranking by the model retrieves more low birth weight births than random ranking, which is a description of retrospective ranking only.

**Limitations.** The dataset release contains no ethics approval or consent statement; a request was sent to the producers on 21 October 2026. A newer version of the dataset exists on Zenodo, and this study stays on version 1 because the specification and every count were frozen against its checksum. It is one public Tanzanian dataset, with no facility or geographic identifier, so neither external nor geographic validation is possible. The development partition holds {dev_events} events, so only differences of roughly the detectable size could be seen. Haemoglobin at visit two is recorded for a minority of pregnancies. The pulse missingness association reflects recording practice and cannot be separated from differences between clinics. The outcome is birth weight recorded under the care actually given, and nothing here shows that acting on a prediction would change it. The held out partition has not been evaluated, the Next.js interface and the container image are not built, and the prototype is a demonstration on synthetic cases that has not been validated for any pregnancy.
